title: TVA water–energy workflow
summary: HEADWATER forecasts feed high-resolution downscaling, Yang’s LSTM water-availability model, and Georgia Tech’s economic assessment. VISTA coordinates the model handoffs and records the evidence.

stages.title: HEADWATER prediction
stages.description: Provide forecast precipitation, air temperature and runoff for the TVA region. Preserve forecast timing and ensemble information through the workflow.
input: Earth-system simulations and seasonal forecast products
output: Air temperature (T, or TMAX/TMIN where supplied)
Forecast issue, valid time and ensemble member IDs
stages.targetResolution: 25 km handoff in the TRITON discussion
stages.integrationNote: The slides describe residual/probability maps. A physical-variable reconstruction and an agreed handoff contract are needed before downstream model execution.

stages.title: Reconstruction & downscaling
stages.description: Reconstruct physical scenarios from the forecast maps and historical references, then downscale regional information for the TVA domains.
input: Forecast issue, valid time and member IDs
output: High-resolution physical precipitation and air-temperature fields
Runoff fields prepared for the downstream model contract
stages.integrationNote: The supplied slides name a 1 km target. They do not establish that a runnable downscaling skill is installed in this VISTA project.

stages.title: LSTM water availability
stages.description: Use Yang’s saved LSTM model to estimate weekly TVA site water availability from prepared basin forcing. The app’s recorded examples expose predictions, reference values and provenance.
input: Prepared basin-week precipitation, temperature and runoff
Static basin attributes required by the chosen model
Target week and twelve preceding weeks
Matched input metadata and frozen checkpoint
output: Input-quality flags and a run summary

sourceRefs.message: User-specified LSTM stage in the TVA workflow

stages.integrationNote: ELF means Estimated Local Flow. Site quantities can be local, incremental or allocated flows, so interpret each site’s reference definition before deriving plant inflow or aggregating across sites. A loaded VISTA skill and a verified runtime are separate from recorded-result availability.

stages.title: Economic assessment
stages.description: Deliver plant-level water records to Georgia Tech for assessment of generation, cost and risk, using agreed scientific and economic assumptions.
input: Plant and economic data supplied by the partner
output: Risk metrics, to be agreed with Georgia Tech
stages.targetResolution: Plant level / daily or weekly records

sourceRefs.message: Georgia Tech is responsible for economic assessment

stages.integrationNote: Economic outputs require Georgia Tech’s model/interface and agreed metrics. The app does not invent costs, generation impacts or risk estimates from an LSTM prediction alone.

branches.title: TRITON hydraulics
branches.description: Add hydraulic detail near plants where the economic handoff needs depth, stage or section discharge.
branches.integrationNote: TRITON is an additional hydraulic path. The discussion explicitly leaves TVA readiness, routing needs and an agentic skill open.

branches.title: RiTHyMs water temperature
branches.description: Provide river temperature near plants when Georgia Tech’s assessment requires thermal effects.
input: Appropriate flow for the model domain
output: A future reservoir/release-temperature path with CE-QUAL-W2
branches.integrationNote: The discussion identifies reservoir setup and CE-QUAL-W2 as later work. These capabilities are distinct from the LSTM water-availability model.

handoff.title: Plant data interface
fields: Water quantity with units and quantity definition
handoff.note: Agree the plant mapping, time aggregation, flow meaning and metrics before Georgia Tech evaluates economic impacts.

sources.title: From HEADWATER forecasts to plant-level water–energy impacts
User clarification: HEADWATER, downscaling, Yang’s LSTM and Georgia Tech economic assessment

disclosures: Workflow cards describe the project design. Installed skills and their count come from the selected live VISTA project.
The included LSTM results are recorded historical examples. HEADWATER, downscaling and economic assessment are not claimed as live executions.
The TRITON discussion permits a first demonstration with clearly labeled selected historical inputs and synthetic scenario assumptions.
The earlier discussion names ORBIT/LANDSIM under prediction and RiTHyMs/RiverWare under impact models. The current four-stage spine follows the user’s later HEADWATER/LSTM/Georgia Tech clarification.
